title: Counterflow heat exchanger: the log-mean temperature difference
caption: Hot oil cools from 150 to 90 °C while water flowing the other way warms from 20 to 70 °C. The two ends see ΔT₁ = 150 − 70 = 80 K and ΔT₂ = 90 − 20 = 70 K. The driving difference is not their plain average: ΔT_lm = (ΔT₁ − ΔT₂)/ln(ΔT₁/ΔT₂) = 74.9 K, the value that goes in Q = UAΔT_lm.
alt: Graph of fluid temperature along the exchanger: the hot oil line falling from 150 to 90 °C and the cold water line, running the other way, from 70 down to 20 °C, with the gap 80 K at one end and 70 K at the other.
description: The horizontal axis is the fractional distance along the exchanger; the vertical axis is the temperature in °C.
Hot oil enters at x = 0 at 150 °C and leaves at x = 1 at 90 °C.
Water enters at x = 1 at 20 °C and leaves at x = 0 at 70 °C (counterflow).
The gap between them is 80 K at x = 0 and 70 K at x = 1; ΔT_lm = 10/ln(80/70) = 74.9 K.
